incidents.name: Tornado Cash governance takeover via mutated proposal
incidents.notes: Not a defect in Tornado's deployed code: proposal 20 passed the DAO's normal vote-and-execute path with legitimately delegated TORN, and Governance.execute() delegatecalled the proposal exactly as designed - the attacker had merely self-destructed and CREATE2-redeployed the proposal contract with hidden code after voting closed, minting 1.2M votes to sybil addresses and then draining ~483k TORN from the governance vault.

sources.ref: onchain review: Governance proxy 0x5efda50f22d34f262c29268506c5fa42cb56a1ce created 2020-12-18 by 0x4e7b3769921c8dfbdb3d1b4c73558db079a180c7 (Tornado deployer), unrelated to attack sender 0x592340957ebc9e4afb0e9af221d06fdddf789de9; 2 EIP-1967 Upgraded events, the last on 2022-02-21 to implementation 0xa9689ed4a82a288e267b11ae8fe137fb4cb2177e, so the executing code was ~453 days old; the recorded tx calls execute(20) directly on the Governance proxy and emits ProposalExecuted(20); the attacker's sybil delegations were set up two days earlier from 0x092123663804f8801b9b086b03b98d706f77bd59; classified governance-design rather than code-bug because the mutated contract sat outside the victim - Governance itself behaved to spec - though a codehash pin at proposal creation (as Audius Governance has) would have blocked it
